question: What primary dual-protection benefit do condoms offer in clinical nursing practice?

options.A: Prevention of pregnancy and iron-deficiency anemia
options.B: Prevention of unintended pregnancies and sexually transmitted infections
options.C: Treatment of chronic hypertension and pelvic inflammatory disease
options.D: Enhancement of hormonal balance and fertility rates

explanation: Condoms act as dual-protection barrier methods that simultaneously prevent unintended pregnancies and reduce the transmission of STIs like HIV. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h1)

question: Why are condoms considered highly accessible in primary healthcare settings?

options.A: They require a surgical procedure for placement
options.B: They are only available via specialist medical prescription
options.C: They require no medical prescription or complex clinical screening
options.D: They can only be distributed by senior consultant physicians

explanation: Condoms do not require a prescription or medical screening, making them universally accessible for community distribution and primary care. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h1)

question: Which material is most commonly used for manufacturing standard male condoms due to its high elasticity?
explanation: Latex is the most common material used for male condoms because it provides high elasticity and reliable barrier protection. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h2)

question: What is a distinct structural feature of a female (internal) condom?

options.A: It contains a solid metal spring inside the shaft
options.B: It features an inner ring for cervical placement and an outer ring remaining outside the vagina
options.C: It must be inflated with air prior to insertion
options.D: It relies entirely on adhesive tape to stay in place

explanation: Female condoms feature an inner ring to secure the device near the cervix and an outer ring that stays outside the vagina to protect external genitalia. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism of action of barrier methods like condoms?

options.A: Altering the female hormonal endocrine feedback loop
options.B: Physically blocking sperm entry and preventing direct mucosal contact with infectious fluids
options.C: Causing systemic destruction of all circulating white blood cells
options.D: Thickening cervical mucus through chemical hormone release

explanation: Condoms work purely through a mechanical action that blocks sperm entry and prevents direct contact with infectious body fluids and lesions. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h3)

question: How do condoms protect against sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: By stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies
options.B: By acting as an impermeable shield preventing contact between genital lesions and infectious fluids
options.C: By releasing localized antibiotics into the bloodstream
options.D: By raising the core body temperature to kill pathogens

explanation: Condoms form an impermeable physical shield that stops direct skin-to-skin contact and fluid exchange between sexual partners. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h3)

question: Why is it important to pinch the tip of a male condom during application?

options.A: To inflate it like a balloon for testing
options.B: To expel trapped air and leave space for semen collection
options.C: To activate the built-in spermicidal lubricant
options.D: To seal the open end tightly against the pubic bone

explanation: Pinching the tip removes trapped air pockets that could cause the condom to burst and creates necessary space to collect ejaculate. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h4)

question: At what point during sexual activity should a male condom be put on?

options.B: After initial genital contact has taken place
options.C: Before any genital contact occurs on an erect penis
options.D: Only when the partner requests birth control

explanation: Condoms must be applied to an erect penis before any genital contact happens to prevent exposure to pre-ejaculatory fluid and sperm. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h4)

question: Which type of lubricant causes the degradation and tearing of latex condoms?
explanation: Oil-based lubricants break down the structural integrity of latex, making it prone to tearing and rendering it ineffective. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h5)

question: What is a consequence of using two male condoms simultaneously during intercourse?

options.A: Enhanced contraceptive efficacy and double protection
options.B: Friction between the two condoms leading to breakage
options.C: Automatic prevention of all known viral infections
options.D: Prolonged duration of the sexual act

explanation: Wearing two condoms creates friction between them, causing the materials to rub against each other and easily break. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h5)

question: Which of the following is a primary clinical advantage of condom use?

options.B: They offer dual protection against pregnancy and STIs with no systemic hormonal side effects
options.C: They regulate the female menstrual cycle for up to five years
options.D: They eliminate the need for user cooperation during intercourse

explanation: Condoms are non-hormonal and provide dual protection against both STIs and unintended pregnancy, making them uniquely advantageous. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h6)

question: What is considered a major limitation of condom use in family planning?

options.A: They cause permanent infertility after discontinuation
options.B: They require continuous, correct user compliance for every single act of intercourse
options.C: They must be surgically implanted by a registered nurse

explanation: Condoms depend entirely on correct and consistent use by the individual every time, which makes them vulnerable to human error. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h6)

question: What is an important teaching strategy for nurses when educating clients on condom use?

options.A: Relying solely on written pamphlets without verbal discussion
options.B: Using anatomical models to demonstrate correct application techniques
options.C: Discouraging questions to maintain strict clinical confidentiality
options.D: Administering a written examination before distribution

explanation: Demonstrating application techniques using anatomical models helps ensure the client fully understands the correct psychomotor steps. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h7)

question: How do nurses contribute to community health regarding barrier methods beyond direct counseling?

options.A: By performing surgical sterilizations in rural health posts
options.B: By managing commodity security and ensuring accessible distribution stocks
options.C: By manufacturing latex materials locally in the clinic
options.D: By legally mandating condom use for all adult citizens

explanation: Nurses support public health by managing distribution stocks and ensuring reliable access to barrier methods for the community. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T018#GNS226_U6_T018_h7)
